Hi Olivia — great context, and congrats on the upcoming launch. We've seen similar ramps for other customers and have a couple of standard paths that minimize bill shock while keeping unit economics aligned. High level:

1) Short-term bridge voucher: one-time credit equal to ~20% of the estimated uplift spend, refundable against usage over a 2–3 month ramp window. This preserves your committed tier and buys time for accurate forecasting.

2) Stepped co-term discounting: if you agree to annualize to a December co-term, we can offer graduated discount bands for the first 6 months of uplift (e.g., 10% on the first +25% uplift bucket, 5% on the next +25%).

3) Usage-triggered auto-tiering: we can add an automatic protection rule that, once sustained uplift exceeds threshold X for 28 days, a pre-negotiated rate table takes effect (prevents surprise overages).

I'm attaching a worksheet with worked examples (see Mediaport_Renewal_Worksheet.xlsx). Before I propose a formal amendment I need to run a quick pricing check with the commercial team — looping in Marissa to help with co-term language and Ben for discount levers.

Would you prefer a one-line amendment (credit + pro-rate) or a slightly longer addendum with tiered pricing?

Best,

Lauren — quick thoughts:

- Voucher sizing: 20% of uplift spend for 3 months is reasonable for a high-trust renewal — treat as one-off credit (non-recurring) tied to usage; require signed acknowledgement so it isn't treated as discount precedent.
- Margin guardrails: limit vouchers to accounts with >6 months of steady usage and require CSM monitoring; if ramp looks permanent we shift to a tiered uplift schedule at renewal.
- Co-term mechanics: prefer a pro-rated add-on bucket (clearly called out in the amendment) rather than re-pricing existing committed capacity; keeps base ARR clean.
- Documentation: I can draft an internal approval note and a 1-page amendment template.

If Marissa signs off on the legal phrasing I'm good to green-light the voucher.
